guide.instructions: Colloquial Kolkata / West Bengal Bengali (cholito bhasha) as actually spoken in Kolkata, not Bangladeshi forms (e.g. jol not pani, mashi/pishi, etc.). The learner cannot read the script and does not want to learn it: the Romanization field is the answer they study; the Bengali field is the script for reference only. Use casual, intuitive romanization without diacritics (amar, khide, jabo, korchi). Informal register only: use tumi forms, never formal apni forms. Mix single words with short everyday phrases. For verbs and verb phrases, include a smattering of tenses as separate cards (e.g. 'I eat' / 'I ate' / 'I will eat' / 'I am eating'), and mark the tense in the English front when it would otherwise be ambiguous. Use Notes for a word-by-word breakdown or literal meaning and any useful grammar point, kept to one line.
